subject: Clarify invoicing cadence, upfront commit and tax residency for Avery Order Form
messages:
From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@averysystems.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@averysystems.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: draft order form (redlines attached) - invoicing / commits

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for sending the draft. Attached is our redline (Avery_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf) with three commercial questions we need clarity on before legal signs off:

1) Invoice cadence & payment term — your draft calls for monthly invoices in arrears with a single yearly minimum commit. We usually invoice quarterly or require an upfront payment for committed capacity. Can you propose options (monthly in arrears, quarterly in advance with quarterly true-up, or 50% upfront + 50% quarterly)?
2) Minimum commit billing — will the committed tokens be invoiced up-front, or billed as-usage with a true-up? Also need definition of how unused committed units are handled at quarter/year end.
3) Tax residency — we need Redwood to confirm tax registration and if you will issue VAT invoices (we are EU entity for some lines, US for others). I attached our tax residency form.

We want to avoid contract back-and-forth with finance/legal — curious what your standard for enterprise is and what flexibility you have on net terms.

Best,
Nina Patel
Sr. Procurement Manager, Avery Systems
Avery Systems | procurement@averysystems.com

Attachment: Avery_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf (PDF, 422KB)
Attachment: Avery_Tax_residency_form.xlsx (Excel, 18KB)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@averysystems.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: draft order form (redlines attached) - invoicing / commits

Nina — thanks for the clear redline and the tax form. Tagging Monica (Finance) and Lauren (Sales Ops) to align on the billing mechanics; cc'ing Karthik for pricing schedule context.

At a high level, our enterprise playbook supports three common configurations — listing pros/cons so we can settle quickly:

- Monthly in arrears (Net 30):
  * Invoicing frequency: monthly; true-up annually for minimum commits.
  * Cashflow: lower upfront for you, higher working capital for us.
  * Use-case: when usage is variable and legal prefers no upfront.

- Quarterly in advance w/ quarterly true-up (Net 30/45):
  * Invoice at quarter start for committed units; quarter-end true-up for over/under usage billed/credited.
  * Reduces risk on our side while not requiring full-year prepay.

- 50% upfront, 50% quarterly (hybrid):
  * Upfront to reserve capacity + quarterly reconciliation.
  * Preferred for large minimum commits (> $250k ARR).

From Redwood's perspective we typically do quarterly in advance for mid-enterprise customers with a quarterly true-up. If Avery prefers monthly in arrears, we can accept that on the condition of either a modest onboarding fee or a small pricing premium for the committed units to offset forecast risk.

On tax: we will need Avery's completed residency form to confirm VAT handling. Monica — can you confirm whether we can accept quarterly advance invoices as part of standard order form and whether net terms should be 30 vs 45 for this deal? Also flag any approvals needed for an upfront 50% payment.

Next steps I propose: Monica to confirm acceptance of quarterly advance + proposed wording for unused committed units; Lauren to prepare updated pricing schedule for the three options and send back to Nina with a trackable summary. If Avery pushes back on upfront, we can default to monthly in arrears with a 3% pricing uplift for the commit.

Thanks — I want to keep momentum this week so we don't push into Q1 legal queue.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:42:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: draft order form (redlines attached) - invoicing / commits

Rishi / Lauren — quick finance take after reviewing the redline and the three options. TL;DR: accept quarterly in advance with quarter-end true-up as Redwood standard for this deal, but we can support monthly in arrears if Avery signs a 12-month minimum and either: (a) 50% upfront or (b) 3% price uplift.

Detailed comments to include in Order Form language (suggested edits):
- Commit billing: "Customer will prepay for committed units at the start of each quarter. Usage in excess of committed units will be invoiced at the contractual overage rate at quarter-end; unused committed units may be carried forward for one subsequent quarter only, then expire."
- Upfront vs arrears: "If Customer selects monthly-in-arrears billing, Customer agrees to a 3% premium on committed-unit prices OR an onboarding fee equal to one month of committed spend."
- Net terms: recommend Net 45 for quarterly-in-advance invoices; Net 30 if customer opts for monthly-in-arrears (we can be flexible if legal approves).
- Taxes: "Customer is responsible for VAT/GST; Redwood will issue VAT invoices where Redwood is registered in the applicable jurisdiction. Customer must submit completed tax residency documentation prior to first invoice to determine VAT handling."

I've attached our tax form template for Avery to complete (Avery_Tax_residency_form.xlsx). Also, if Avery needs a PO on file, advise Lauren and we'll create an invoice sequence that splits committed vs overage lines for easy PO mapping.

If Avery pushes on no-upfront + Net 60, we'll escalate to Revenue Ops and sales leadership. For now, I'll prepare clean contract language and a 1-page summary of the three commercial options for Nina.

— Monica Patel
Director, Finance Operations | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

Rishi / Monica — thanks for the options and the clear language. Internal finance reviewed and their position: Avery prefers monthly in arrears (operationally easier), but we cannot do an onboarding fee. We are comfortable with a 3% premium on committed-unit pricing to offset your risk.

Two asks before we sign:
1) Please add explicit language that unused committed units may be credited at the quarter-end true-up (we prefer carry-forward for two quarters instead of one).
2) Confirm Redwood will issue VAT invoices for EU-registered subscriptions — we'll return the tax residency form this week.

If Redwood is agreeable to (a) monthly-in-arrears + 3% premium and (b) carry-forward for two quarters, we can instruct legal to execute the MSA/order form next week. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Carlos Mendez
